subject.title: feat: let plugin tools yield turns

question: Should the permanent Plugin SDK contract use a distinct yield-capability declaration, or should every sequential tool intentionally become direct-only under Tool Search and Code Mode?
rationale: Both choices can implement safe turn handoff, but they define different long-lived plugin compatibility and catalog behavior that cannot be selected from tests alone.

options.title: Separate yield capability
options.body: Add an explicit descriptor capability for yield-capable tools, preserve catalog behavior for other sequential tools, and land after focused compatibility coverage.

options.title: Accept sequential-implies-direct
options.body: Approve the broader contract intentionally and add upgrade proof documenting that all existing sequential tools become model-visible.

options.title: Pause for interaction roadmap
options.body: Defer the SDK addition until the broader structured-interaction work establishes the shared runtime-control contract.

recommendation.title: Separate yield capability
recommendation.body: Add an explicit descriptor capability for yield-capable tools, preserve catalog behavior for other sequential tools, and land after focused compatibility coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is a public Plugin SDK and tool-catalog product contract spanning agent runtime and plugin author behavior.
